t:
Yakhch is a unique land in the sense that it's the only allod that has changed a lot over the years. It was once a typical desert allod, but then the Great Tree was planted there.

It changed the desert - it sucked out excess salt, consolidated the sands, and raised the water level. Mixed forests began to grow on the allod, and a different fauna appeared.

Now it's more of a typical allod from the middle latitudes than the hot desert of the south.

[Map missing]

Yakhch was once an ordinary desert allod, but it was here that the druids came in their time, having decided to try planting a seed of the Great Tree in one of the oases. The Tree changed the landscape of Yakhch profoundly. Where there was desert, mighty forests — a true taiga — now rise. The climate changed too: there is more rain and it is colder overall. Today this land is a source of timber, which the Xadaganians ship to various parts of their state.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
[Map missing]

The Great Mage of this allod was the wise Gramon de Doucer, a disciple of the elven mages of old, second in power only slightly to Skrakan. He united everyone who found themselves on his allod after the Night of Woe into a single, largest House, and revived the tradition of the Great Houses, in which the remaining Eight Great Houses now began to take part. Yoggor itself is a rather unusual place: a majestic forest full of enormous trees. Most of the elves live in their own castles, scattered in great numbers across the allod. Although only elves inhabit this allod, there are also those who can pose a threat to lone travellers — various mindless creatures such as giant spiders and mantises. But everything comes to an end, and a terrible fate befell Yoggor too: an extraordinarily deadly spell that changed the familiar way of life on the allod, darkening it with gloom. After the deadly spell, it changed its name to Nocturne.
f:
The House de Desirae has won several times; its present success is owed to Prince Dakkar, the son of our king. It was Prince Dakkar who restored the prestige of necromancy among the Elves, which led the Conclave to lift the last bans on practising it. After that Ball, however, unpleasant events followed: the House de Doucer, or rather its Head, Armando, acted with extraordinary baseness and brought about the death of the prince's bride, a flagrant violation of the rules of the Great Game. Louis de Desirae seized on this to declare the House de Doucer outlaw and confiscated its home allod, Nocturn.
So the House de Desirae now owns two allods: little Tenebra and vast Nocturn.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; mines are located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Aha! So this story caught your interest too? It used to be our Imperial mine. Hundreds of goblins, under the watchful guidance and loud cursing of the foremen, dug up valuable strategic resources there! Well, there were some other natives too, who lived in the caves — kobolds and mountainfolk — but by special order of the Committee number... oh, I don't remember, 123\16-BIS or something, all the natives were made honorary citizens of the Empire and obliged to labor for the good of the country. And those rascals didn't want to work! No notion of discipline whatsoever. No faith in the bright future! Lazybones! They conspired with one terribly clever goblin — Ghim the Greedy, they call him — won the trolls over to their side, and drove out all the foremen, engineers and bookkeepers! Now they have something there that's either a monarchy or a commune, and Ghim is their boss. He caved in all the tunnels, raked up a pile of gold for himself, and sits there chuckling — he has beaten the Empire, you see, the scoundrel. But it's not all cakes and ale for the cat! There are still goblins on the island loyal to the Empire, a squad of bang-bang demolishers. They'll blast a tunnel through any rock! With their help you'll easily reach the lair of that separatist and plunderer of the people's economy, Ghim the Greedy. Whatever treasure you find is yours. And deliver Ghim a stern reprimand, on behalf of the whole working class, with an entry in his skull. The Empire will not forget you!

Bosses: Wick, Stakh Quickpick, Stonegnawer, Ghim the Greedy.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, remnants of June mechanisms and ghosts of the June.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Young adventurers are firmly convinced that where there are June ruins, there are countless treasures. Seasoned heroes have learned that in ruins you can sometimes find a hoard, but more often trouble. And the most experienced know that most ruins hold neither treasures nor monsters: small wonder, since they have been there themselves and have already taken care of both. Is there anything on Altan Tepek? I don't know: the islet is placed very awkwardly, nothing but reefs all around. We sailed all the way round it, looked it over through a spyglass, but found nowhere to land. Still, it's a curious place: it looks like a tropical forest, yet there's snow everywhere, frost-covered palms stick up, and the wind howls over the frozen jungle. I thought I noticed some movement, but I never made out who it was: kobold marauders, maybe, or June undead. What, you want to dig about in the old ruins? Well, if you do manage to land, tell me afterwards who was roaming there and why everything froze!

Bosses: Frostmount, Jasper Defender, Metztlitotec, Ayateotle.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater and Avilon.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, belongs to followers of Tep.

Story:

Sorbas Logey, a senior laboratory assistant at the ZIT, was testing a technology for transferring an essence into mechanisms other than Zem bodies. When the ship of their expedition moored at this island, it was attacked by an Astral Monster. After his death on this island, in accordance with his technology, he moved into the body of his robot, the "Astral Guardian"; and the island holds a huge number of undead (although, because of the gift of Tensess, he ought to have ended up in Purgatory). To help sort this out, one must fight one's way into the depths of the island and kill "Little Skull", an undead draconid, clearing the island of the dead along the way. Since after the draconid's death the assistant still remained in the guardian's body, he asked us to reach the center of the island and try to get to the bottom of it there, for in the guardian's body he is weak and cannot get there himself. At the center of the island there turns out to be a place of power and a Cultist Rhetor; after defeating him we return to the guardian. Sorbas says that this place works on the same principle as Tep's pyramid, but now (apparently after the ritual was interrupted) he can go back to Purgatory again.

Bosses: Little Skull, Cultist Rhetor.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mostly by trolls and lamias.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Perhaps you have already come across creatures touched by the Astral. Under its influence they change, and more often than not they change for the worse...

The Astral Horn is just such a creature. It is a unicorn turned into a dangerous monster. Even reaching it will not be easy, let alone defeating it. But there is something I do know… Once you find the island of the Astral Horn, you will have to hack your way through the astral crystals. Quite literally. You need the Hammer of Pain. You can obtain the hammer itself by defeating Splasher, a dangerous water elemental. Then, fighting the granite trolls, you will collect Shards of Pain. The power hidden in them will let you charge your weapon with magic. That can be done in the June ruins guarded by a cyclops nicknamed Stomper. And only once you have that weapon will you be able to break through the magic shield barring the way to the Horn's lair. I do not know what awaits you there. Be ready for anything. All that is known is that the Horn is not easy to find: it knows how to hide.

Bosses: Splasher, Stomper, Astral Horn.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Gallery: None :/

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph and the Dragon Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a pirate lair.

Story:

We arrive at a camp of Free Traders who want to destroy the pirate lair that has settled here. According to their plan, to drive the pirates away one must kill their leader and the goblins, so that the rest will slaughter one another fighting for power. Those who remain the Free Traders can finish off themselves. Naturally, we do all of this for them. Along the way we also catch fish for an Orc and kill a hydra that roars at night and keeps a delicate Elf maiden from sleeping.

Bosses: Hydra, Pirate Ataman.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Wasteland, closest to Yazes Shard.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Demons.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Black Rock... You'll recognize it the moment you approach the island! A lifeless shard of bare stone, gnawed by demonic fangs. It's simply swarming with demons! As far as I know, the Black Rock is all that remains of the allod of the House de Blizare after the Night of Astral Portals. The House de Blizare suffered enormous losses that night. Almost all their mages died in battle; the Great Mage lost his nerve and prepared to open a portal to Kvatoh, which finally broke the fighting spirit of the defenders. The elves fled, leaving their allod to be torn apart by the demons. However, for some reason I can't understand, the allod turned out to be extraordinarily resistant to the effects of the astral. They say the blood of the elven martyrs who defended their home to the last is the cause... But I don't believe it! Elves are deceitful and selfish creatures who know nothing of heroic self-sacrifice. Although by their standards such a death would surely count as beautiful. In short, the Black Rock is now a piece of land crawling with demons. There are as many of them as fleas on a goblin! So I strongly advise you not even to go near this island. An armada of demons is not the enemy you want to run into in the astral!

Bosses: Gryzl, Bonegrinder, Hornbearer, Sparky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Zem.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Blood Countess... She who bathes in the blood of young girls to preserve her own beauty... Do you really want to hear this story? I'll tell you straight: it's disgusting. The Blood Countess's real name is Yasskul Bathory. I knew her personally — a pleasant lady and an outstanding researcher. But she had a thing about her appearance. Bathory, once the most beautiful of the rulers of Hickut, seized on any chance to regain her lost beauty. And, unfortunately, she found one... Thanks to her knowledge of ancient blood magic she was able to rejuvenate her body... and kill her soul! Hundreds of ruined women, rivers of blood steeped in terrible spells — that was the price. Bathory was outlawed and sentenced to death, but she managed to escape! Rumor has it that the Blood Countess took refuge on one of the astral islands. She has a whole estate there, with well-drilled and devoted servants. The horrors and debauchery that go on there would drive even a battle-hardened warrior mad! Beware the Blood Countess, if you don't want to become one of her slaves and end your life as a bloodless body on a laboratory floor.

Bosses: Yaver Nadashti, Rolling Hill, Mechanical Watchman, Yasskul Bathory.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: During internal testing of the island, an amusing bug appeared on it: a pigeon grew to the size of a boss. In the end it was decided to immortalize it and make it a mascot named Gosha. Now it can be met in various places across Sarnaut.

t:
Climate: Temperate, cursed land.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by merchants and a circus troupe.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, I know that place. A rather gloomy little place, I must say. Once there was a circus there, a perfectly ordinary circus, with clowns, acrobats and a trained bear with a balalaika. But the place was not popular. Who would fly through the danger-filled Astral just to look at some jesters? And so the circus fell into complete neglect. And then three men turned up there, calling themselves professors, specialists in dreams and fantasies. They patched up the old circus buildings and sent invitations to their Carnival to anyone who wished to come. The masters of the Carnival guarantee the fulfilment of the most cherished desires, the rosiest dreams and the most incredible fantasies. As far as I'm concerned, they are all charlatans, every last one. They don't take money from anyone, by the way, which is very strange. Now if they wanted to line their pockets, then the point of such promises would at least be understandable. For now all I can advise you is — keep your ears pricked!

Bosses: Dread, Heat, Red Beard, Harlequin.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Desert, closest to the Den.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Tep's cultists.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

During one of my expeditions I was... hm... unlucky enough to visit the Tomb Isle. On my first visit it was a deserted place keeping the peace of one of Tep's Pyramids. My second visit was a vivid confirmation of the sad fact that Tep's cult has been restored. Now his followers rule the Tomb. They use stone elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I do not know what they are looking for there — my companions and I, many of whom were seriously wounded in the fight, had to leave the island in a hurry. I am sure nothing good can be expected from the activities of Tep's followers. I ask you to find that island and put an end to the cultists' doings. You will have to fight both them and their stone elementals. And most importantly — destroy Isdes, Tep's high priest, who leads the excavation of the Pyramid.

Bosses: Variant 1: Tep's Prelate, Tailstabber, Isdes. Variant 2: Longbelly, Tep's Prelate, Isdes, Sefnut.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by smugglers and the like.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Thanks be to Yasker, the Empire has no shortage of places for cultured recreation. If you like, go to the cinema; if you like, to a museum or a library; if you like, take a trip to a sanatorium, or to the Summer Atoll. Not enough excitement in your life — then play the sports lottery! And yet even here we still have elements for whom such entertainments are not enough; they want something hotter and more forbidden. And this in the Empire — as for the debauchery that goes on abroad, I simply keep silent! Well, as long as there is demand, there will be supply. In short, one crafty goblin found a stable islet in the Astral and set up an arena for gladiatorial fights there. Almost like on Yazes — only without demons, but with gambling and young ladies of dubious reputation. What riff-raff does not hang about there: mercenaries, and smugglers, and slave traders... They drink, place bets, cut each other for nothing. Shame and disgrace! Decent people have no business there, mark my words.

Bosses: Mussle, Spartacus, Cerbarath, Caligula.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.
f: Based on the Shard of Umoir.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a hunting estate.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Cinderland... Yes, there's no other name for that islet now. And yet once it was the finest hunting reserve in the Empire! They say the Great Yasker himself liked to shoot ducks or run down a deer in that reserve. And the local forester, Kuzmich, was a fine drinking companion — sometimes we'd get so plastered with him that in the morning we forgot which of us was the forester and which the traveler. Hm, those were the days... And now there's nothing there but charred trunks sticking up and rabid beasts running about. Curse that mad Arisen Zem! And at first they received him as an honored guest. Why, an outstanding scholar had decided to pursue his research in the quiet of the forest! They arranged every comfort for him, you understand — a laboratory in the woods, peace and bliss. He worked away, clinking his flasks... But Kuzmich, kind soul, decided to find himself a drinking companion. He could hardly drink with the bears, after all? And he took to dropping in on this mage, to chat about science over a bottle or two. And Kuzmich's hooch is mighty strong! Kuzmich was fine, he has a cast-iron throat and a steel liver, but the wizard, blast him, drank himself into the horrors. And in his drunken state he went completely off his rocker, foundations and all. The swine set the forest on fire! He imagined himself the Fireborn, the Great Fire Mage, lord of flame, anchor up his stern! And that was it, the reserve was done for — for he really is a Great mage, so now the forest there burns but does not burn up, the animals blaze but do not roast, and the most terrible thing is that the spirit of the forest, old Oakwarden, fell under his spell and serves him. And Kuzmich has taken to drinking out of grief; he recognizes no one, just swills vodka without ever sobering up. I tried to bring him to his senses, but he punched me in the face and kicked me out of his hut, where a pack of fire wolves was already waiting. They chased me all the way to my ship and burnt such a hole in my trousers — it's a shame to say. At least they didn't singe my hide. So if you mean to pay a visit to the Cinderland that is left of the reserve, don't forget to take a fire extinguisher with you — believe me, it's blazing there good and proper.

Bosses: Kuzmich, Oakwarden, Volkh, Fireborn.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a Kanian settlement.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know the place. Only I strongly advise against flying there! On that island there's a whole village of religious fanatics. Unwashed peasants who, not so long ago, meekly grew turnips for the Kanian soldiery have imagined themselves heaven knows what. They've rejected faith in the Light, not to mention the veneration of Saints Nezeb and Skrakan, and worship some kind of nature spirits. And their leader is the magus Jaromir. It was he, the bearded lunatic, who incited all the peasants to revolt! He's completely addled the village men's heads with his tales about the faith of their ancestors, the greatness of ancient Kania, the glorious Traditions... No, honoring traditions is sacred. But with some sense! We're building mana stations and underground railways, the League is treading on our heels in developing industry, and they're still living in the last millennium. A wild people, in a word — not like us, the enlightened citizens of the great Empire. So if the road leads you to Clear Mountain, get ready to fight the whole village at once. And the local bogatyrs too. Alexei, Ivan and Vladislav, hulking brutes — step out of line and they'll hammer you into the ground up to your ears. But if you manage to defeat Jaromir himself, maybe the peasants will come to their senses and stop grabbing every stranger and throwing him into the astral...

Bosses: Aunt Agafya, Vladislav the Cruel, Prokopy, Jaromir.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: Until recently this rich mine belonged to Umoir merchants. That is, they thought it belonged to them — but in fact the Mistress lives in the depths of the island to this day. If she wants, she shares her riches; if she doesn't, she sends misfortune. And so she stopped wanting to. Whether people angered her with their greed or failed to show her respect, but now wolves and bears roam the village instead of miners. I wouldn't fly there: what if the Mistress gets angry with me too! Her riches in the depths are, of course, countless — only she guards them so well that you can't get near them!

Climate: Temperate, closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Until recently this rich mine belonged to Umoir merchants. That is, they thought it belonged to them — but in fact the Mistress lives to this day in the depths of the island. If she wishes, she shares her riches; if she doesn't, she sends misfortune. Well, and she stopped wishing. Whether people angered her with their greed or failed to show her due respect, only now wolves and bears roam the village instead of miners. I wouldn't fly there: what if the Mistress gets angry with me too! Her riches in the depths are countless, to be sure — only she guards them so that you can't get near!

Story allod:

For a ritual Velerad needed living gems — prophetic yakhonts, which could be found only on the island of Copper Mountain. It turned out that the island had once belonged to Goldie Nickel, but Goldie had lost it, and the new owner was his brother Zavid Nickel, a greedy, grasping man. Meanwhile disaster had struck the workings: something was frightening the miners to death, and they refused to work. The heroes tried to get to the bottom of it, and they had to pass a difficult path of riddles and trials to reach the local Sovereign — the Mistress of the Local Mountain. She punished Zavid for his greed by turning him to stone, but agreed to give a yakhont on condition that the mine be returned to Goldie and the way to her underground halls be forgotten. Alas, if anything in the world is immortal, it is human greed. Learning of the halls of the Mistress of the Copper Mountain, which were full of precious stones, people fitted out more than one expedition, breaking the agreement. After the ritual Velerad never learned where the Plague had come from. The visions were hazy and incomprehensible.

Bosses: Fire Jumper, Blue Yaga, Mighty Poloz, Mistress of the Copper Mountain.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Addendum: The island was made on the basis of concepts by a player nicknamed Merani. The Servant of Light on the allod is a reference to her.

t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Taiga, closest to Eljune.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, formerly Kanian.

Story:

We are met by the Aviak Elder. He tells us that they (the aviaks) have been guarding this place for a very long time, so that the evil does not get out and so that the strangers who come to this island do not feed the EVIL with strength. The aviak suggests that we go to the guarded borders and see from whom they are protecting the world. We discover banshees and decide they ought to be killed. Besides the ordinary ones, we also defeat an ancient banshee and return. The aviak is amazed at our courage and strength and says that the banshees are apparently scouts, but the shadows by the second bridge are already closer to the source. If you manage to defeat them too, find the spirit of the priest in one of the huts.

We head there, defeat the Shadows and look for the hut with the priest. The Hermit Spirit (the priest) tells us that in the times of the great battles he felt some shadow flying from the depths of the astral, but it could not fly any further. It stopped near our church. That is when it all began: the earth began to rot, the animals changed horribly, shadows began to crawl out. The Kanians left these places, but he, a servant of Tensess, decided to stay, and tried to cleanse these places and drive out the shadows. By his reckoning, his attempts to cope with the evil only helped it to spread.

In his helplessness the aviaks began to help him. He points out to us that the source of the evil lies beyond the church, to the southeast. Arriving at the spot, we discover that the cause of the horrors on this island is a part — the evil part — of the soul of Tensess. And we destroy it.

Bosses: Ancient Banshee, Ancient Shadow, the Dark Side of Tensess.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former Kanian settlement, now inhabited by the undead.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Many have heard the stories of the Silent Hills. An ancient evil awoke in that land, turning the peasants into will-less ghosts. They wandered their lands until brave heroes put an end to their suffering. But in the deep layers of the Astral the Silent Hills have a reflection. That is what an Imperial Warlock chose for his experiments. And he got so carried away that the horrors of old now seem like a children's tale. The villain destroyed the whole people and turned the good inhabitants into an army of the undead. Those hills are no longer Silent, but Dead!

Bosses: Cadaver, Guardian, Murderess, Sarang Fravashi.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: This island belongs to Nomarkh Iblis, an oligarch and inventor. He is a rich and famous man, but not much respected: he is far too fond of inventing schemes to cheat his partners instead of weapons. Only this last time he picked the wrong target: he had the nerve to swindle Yasker himself. Yasker would not swallow the insult, and as soon as his scouts found the island, he sent a whole battalion there. How it all ended, I don't know. Nothing came of it, I think: the imperial soldiers are strong, but a factory stuffed to the rafters with weapons can't be taken in one rush either. We Leaguers have nothing to do there — except perhaps watch the show from afar. Want to make a bet? I wager ten gold that the Imperials won't manage it!

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a laboratory is located here.

Story:
Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

This island belongs to Nomarkh Iblis, an oligarch and inventor. He's a rich man, well known, but not very respected. He's far too fond of inventing schemes to cheat his partners instead of weapons. Only last time he picked the wrong target: he had the gall to swindle Yasker himself. Yasker wouldn't swallow the insult, and as soon as his scouts found the island, he sent a whole battalion there. How it all ended, I don't know. In my opinion, it didn't: the Imperial soldiers are strong, but you can't take a factory stuffed to the roof with weapons in one rush either. We Leaguers have nothing to do there — except maybe watch the show from afar. Want to make a bet? I'll put ten gold on the Imperials not pulling it off!

Story allod:

Catherina sent the Heroes to search for Yelisseus Korolev. And only his old nanny knew where he was. It turned out that Yelisseus had disappeared on the Death Plant island: he had gone there to learn from Nomarkh Iblis, the Oligarch, where to find his beloved Annette. Setting off after Yelisseus, the heroes met on the island Leila Snoop, a Committee operative who had picked up the trail of a sinister conspiracy.

This very Nomarkh Iblis, one of the seven Oligarchs who rule the Free Traders, grew rich on the arms trade. All those turrets, mechanisms and other weapons that have flooded Sarnaut in recent years are his handiwork. But the trouble lay elsewhere. Not long ago Iblis put a new weapon on sale — the Spinners. And on every one of the Spinners he installed a remote-control device. At one fine moment the Spinners were to rise against their owners, and Iblis would become the ruler of all Sarnaut. Leila offered to thwart his plans. Long and bloody was the path through the laboratories and workshops of the Death Plant; the Xadaganian scout herself fell victim (or so it seemed at the time); and Yelisseus was found, whom Iblis had wanted to turn into a mechanical bogatyr. For it turned out that all of Catherina's guard, the bogatyrs, had been remade from heroes, and inside the mechanical bodies were the Sparks of the living. The heroes fought their way out of the dungeons with Yelisseus, finished off Iblis himself, and on his body found documents proving that he had been cooperating with Catherina. She did not deny it, and admitted that she had needed Iblis for his technologies. "Engineers with powerful manatrons, a flying tower, the best shipyard in the world and my mechanical guard — none of this came out of thin air."

Bosses: Yasskul Samekh, Modified Orc, Ghost of Yaver Khess, Polytoc Hexnut.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Xadaganians.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What tricky questions you ask. And do you know that for that sort of thing you can end up in the Committee's dungeons? You see, even after the Cataclysm not all Xadaganians accepted Nezeb's rule. When the industrial revolution began in the Empire, some isolated allods inhabited by Xadaganians did not accept the new doctrine and went on living by the old customs. Dersaadet is just such a place. A shard, so to speak, of the old Empire, frozen in timelessness. There they do not believe in the Light, do not honour the saints of the Trinity Church, but pray to the Almighty in a mosque. Dersaadet is ruled by Sultan Mustapha al Muhad, and his power is boundless. And whoever wants to challenge it will have to deal with loyal janissaries and the magic of a cunning vizier. But if you come to Dersaadet in peace, generous hospitality awaits you, fine wines and delicacies such as the world has never seen!

Bosses: Buzagi Bey, Mehmet Pasha, Rajima, the Serpent-Faced.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, forest creatures and spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

What questions you ask! I'd be glad to forget that island, but I can't...

Long ago Kanian druids brought a sprout of the Great Tree to a lifeless islet and turned barren stone into a truly magnificent forest. I happened to visit it, and I confess without hypocrisy — even in the Empire there are few places whose beauty can compare with that lovely sunny island as it was then. The mentor of the local pagans, the wise Dobroslav Radov, proved a most cordial host and received me, an Imperial, hospitably, disregarding all the differences between our powers! I flew away from the island with a friendly farewell and warm memories of birdsong, crystal-clear lakes, the most delicious birch sap and the rustle of thick foliage. And recently bad news reached me. A giant spider, a vile spawn of the Astral, crept up to the Great Tree under cover of darkness and poisoned it with its venom. All of Dobroslav's followers, and he himself, went mad. Now he is called Zlobinya Yadov, and nothing remains in him of the good-natured sage he once was. Now he and his servants offer bloody sacrifices to the Desecrated Tree! The whole island is overrun with venomous spiders, tirelessly spawned by their mother, the Black Widow. And Blackvenom himself hides somewhere in the dense forest. But if you tear out the hearts of the mad pagans and grant them peace by burning them in cleansing fire, Blackvenom will surely not be slow to appear. And with his death the blight will leave the forest forever. I beg you, cleanse the Desecrated Forest! Kill the Widow and Blackvenom, and perhaps the soul of the man I remember as Dobroslav will find peace...

Bosses: Black Widow, Zlobinya Yadov, Yevstigney Volkov, Blackvenom.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: A quiet little island, an unremarkable one. Seven hero brothers once lived there, whiling away their old age among the forests and marshes. Then some shabby elven House settled there, having fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Plague reached the island, then the head of the House brought his wife — a Kanian, by the way — a present: a wondrous mirror, the work of the ancient June, with a golden frame and a glass of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that: from them you can only expect some trick or a curse. In short, there was no reason to go to that island before, and now it is downright frightening. Although... what if there are hunters willing to get that mirror? For the brave, as everyone knows, the law is not written!

Climate: Tropical. Closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Elven allod, inhabited by the remnants of the elves whom Catherina drove out.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A quiet little island, an inconspicuous one. Seven bogatyr brothers lived there, whiling away their old age among the forests and marshes. Then some shabby elven House settled there — they had fled persecution on Umoir. Only they found no happiness there. First the Plague reached the island, then the head of the House brought his wife — a Kanian, by the way — a little present. A marvelous mirror, a work of the ancient June — a golden frame, and the mirror itself of black obsidian. Well, June treasures are like that — expect nothing from them but some trick or a curse. In short, there was no reason to go to that island before, and now it's downright frightening. Although... what if there are takers who'll want to get that mirror? For the bold, as everyone knows, the law is not written!

Story allod:

The elves began attacking the shipyard where the new ship "Eclipse" was being built, and generally getting in the way in every manner. The heroes had to be sent to deal with them. The heroes routed the elves, and it turned out that they were led by Alir de Tristesse. That same Alir who had been the head of the minor House of Tristesse and the father of that same Annette who had been Yelisseus's beloved. But the elf's mind had sunk into twilight — he only cried out gloomy prophecies. What had happened stirred Yelisseus himself — he had long searched for his beloved, and it turned out that the elves, on leaving Umoir, had gone to the Drowsy Woods. Without long preparation, Yelisseus set off. Alas, the Drowsy Woods proved a grim place. The Plague was raging there in full force, and nothing remained of the elven settlement but ruins. With a heavy heart Yelisseus found Annette's own diary. It emerged that the elf maiden had fled the persecution of her stepmother, the new wife Alir had brought home. And she had fled into the forest, where she found shelter with seven bogatyrs. Yelisseus set off to find them. When all of them had been found, the brothers told the sad news — Annette had died, killed by the machinations of that same wicked Baba Yaga. Yelisseus set off for revenge and fell into a trap; fortunately the heroes managed to save him and finish off the witch. And the cause, as it turned out, was a June artifact, the Mirror. It remained to say farewell to Annette herself. Yelisseus wished to see his beloved one last time as she lay in a crystal coffin. But when he reached that cave, the coffin was shattered, and out of it stepped Annette... Alas, the elf maiden had become a vampire. Yelisseus was full of resolve to save his beloved after all. "Stop! Don't destroy her!.. So that is what the accursed sorceress meant. Annette, my poor beautiful Annette! It wasn't enough for the witch to destroy the one fairer than she — the mad old woman decided to turn her into a monster! I don't believe it is all fated to end like this. If there is a way in the world to lift the curse from her, I will do it. But I dare not ask you for help again — this is my love and my burden. Leave us. And thank you for everything!"

With heavy hearts the heroes left the cursed island.

Bosses: Baba Yaga, Yelisseus, Annette de Tristesse, Evil Mirror.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, where Imperial outlaws have settled.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, I know about that island. How could I not? A decent little place... If you're ready to put up with quacking that doesn't stop for a minute! There's a Kanian village there, and every house has ducks beyond counting. They salt duck, bake it, dry it and sell it. Even the pillow in my cabin is stuffed with local down. It's like lying down to sleep on a cloud... But a misfortune has befallen them. Have you heard about the recent escape from the maximum security zone? No? Strange... It was in all the papers. A whole gang of convicts, mostly orcs and goblins, slaughtered the guards, seized a ship and made off in an unknown direction. They called themselves the "Tribe of the Daring" and set about robbing, wrecking and burning everything in their path. Lawless thugs, what else can I say. They boarded several of our ships, robbed them down to the last frame, and threw the crews overboard. They wiped out an outpost in the far astral root and branch — the Committee's investigators came back from there green as frogs and swearing like cobblers. And the last thing I heard about that gang is that they stumbled upon Duck River Run. Well, the locals are out of luck. I'm afraid even to imagine what lawlessness is going on there now!

Bosses: Torch the Daring, Haze the Daring, Rod the Daring, Chopper the Daring.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Wasteland, part of the Architects' universe.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Architects.

Story:

And they never did manage to finish off the damned Architects. The main attack was broken with the greatest effort, but at one moment those creatures scattered all over the world. Then a captain I know told me: he saw a familiar island in the deep Astral, once so very green, a real oasis. Now it is stark naked. Only those blue spires stick out. And beasts live there. They stare with a dead gaze. Their big eyes glow blue. Ugh, it gives me goosebumps… The Architects must have settled there and are remaking everything again in their own wretched likeness. Oh, if only someone would smash them to pieces…

Bosses: Pteros, Oculus, Arctus, Zero.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a large trading city.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Don't you know? "Where to, where to... To East Overshoe!" — that is how traders used to answer anyone too curious before casting off from the pier. And not without reason — on East Overshoe there was a rich trading city whose inhabitants talked in practically nothing but proverbs. Whatever you ask an Overshoer, he answers you with a saying. It was a rich city, and misfortune passed it by. The Overshoers grew so used to a quiet life that they would say, "we'll start shutting the gates when a crayfish whistles on the mountain". Well, the crayfish waited and waited, and then it whistled. They got what they bargained for. And yet they had been told — let sleeping trouble lie! The other day I flew past East Overshoe — everything has fallen into desolation, not a sound, not a rustle. But who knows what is really going on there? From afar it's just an abandoned city, but, as the saying goes, still waters run deep and devils live in them!

Bosses: Sleeping Trouble, Clop, Byak and Zyrk, the Noon Witch, Raak.

Type: Medium allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian estate.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

There is nothing remarkable about that island. I don't really know much about it. It seems to be a Kanian allod. It is ruled by the illusionist mage Dobrinya Velikov. He calls himself "the Great", though I doubt his strength would really be enough to hold the island. A disagreeable person, I must say... He puffs himself up as if he really were Great, but in fact he is an ordinary fairground conjurer! There is a story that long, long ago a young sorceress, Alla by name, somehow got to that island without any ship at all. A magic whirlwind picked up her house, apparently, and threw it straight there. Along with her little dog and her nail file... There, on the island, Alla met strange but friendly creatures: a talking lion, an ancient lumberjack golem and a living scarecrow. Together with her new friends, having gone through incredible adventures, Alla finally reached the local mage, and he sent the hapless enchantress home. Although personally I suspect that the cause of that journey was not a whirlwind but a bottle of fortified liqueur and the great impressionability of that scatterbrained person, as well as the appetite for sensations of certain chatty scribblers!

Bosses: Brainless Scarecrow, Steel Lumberjack, Cowardly Lion, Dobrinya Velikov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Varied (temperate and wasteland), closest to Coba Plateau (part of the Holy Land island), and also the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; a research base is located here.

Story:

We are met by the base staff, who mention a distress signal in passing but immediately get down to business. Demons have attacked the allod; the base personnel are fighting, but without reinforcements they won't hold out long. An employee tells us, in spite of the secrecy of all the base's work, that a Zem burial has been found on the allod, and that it appeared later than Tep's Plague; as they found out in the course of their research, these Zem turned out to be followers of Tep. During the battle at Asee-Teph the protection fell, and the followers took their secrets to the grave — and it was those that we were looking for. We must find Yaver Matez, the chief Zem scientist at this base, with the help of a Mentaloscope. Making our way past aggressively disposed personnel, we find the scientist. Yaver told us that, according to his theory, the demons are hunting for Tep's knowledge. We must defeat the demon mentors who are trying to extract information from Tep's dead followers. We kill them, and all that remains is to destroy their leader, the Astral Worm.

Bosses: Astral Worm.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Isle of the Edge.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Kanian allod, though vampires of the House de Doucer have settled there alongside the Kanians.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Who would have thought that people and vampires could live in peace anywhere? But, believe it or not, there is such a place! It is called Enoch Isle. Once Enoch was a backwater islet of two villages. And not so long ago vampires who had renounced their creator, Armando de Doucer, arrived on the island. Somehow they came to an agreement with the peasants and receive blood in exchange for their goods, healing magic and other useful things. You won't believe it, but I saw with my own eyes that people and vampires live there in perfect harmony! But everything changed when werewolves appeared on Enoch. A cruel pack of half-sentient beasts invaded Enoch, and peaceful life came to an end. Their leader, the former bandit chieftain Lyut the Bobtailed, swore to devour everyone who does not bow before him. The vampires shut themselves off from the werewolves with magical barriers, closing the passages between the villages, and together with the peasants they hold back the monsters' attacks with their last strength. So if your adventures take you to Enoch, get ready for a fierce battle! Until you manage to clear both villages of werewolves completely, you will not get to their leader.

Bosses: Murk, Paul de Doucer, Vasilissa the Terrible, Lyut the Bobtailed.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Fenia's Island? Ah, that's the old Kanian fortress where those... what do you call them... right, I remember — the feminists! Or femmeists? Anyway, they're women who believe men wrong and oppress them, which has driven them clean out of their minds. No, you tell me — does anyone wrong women in the Empire? It's in the League that folk are completely savage; they even have a saying there, "a hen's no bird, and a woman's no person." Whereas with us she's every bit a person! Only our Imperial ladies run off to that Cloister regularly too... I don't understand why they've turned so against men?! Well, never mind, listen further. Their leader is some Fenia, a mad sorceress who proclaimed herself a goddess incarnate and the patroness of women. She announced that all the evil in the world comes from men, and decided to wage a merciless war on us — on men, that is! And the funniest thing is that some cracked heads actually believed her! Or rather, it was funny right up until they killed every man on the island, and the parts of their bodies — well, the ones that matter most to a man — they... All right, I don't want to talk about it. A friend of mine, Afanasy Nikitov, was there and saw it all with his own eyes. The horrors he told me... He escaped by a miracle! In short, there are no men in the Cloister now. Instead there's a crowd of women of every race, gone feral for lack of male attention and fanatical to the marrow, ready to tear apart any man who ends up on the island. Now there's a paradox — they hate men, yet without men they turn into beasts. No, I'll never understand women. Especially women who reach for a sword at the slightest thing and try to lop off what's most precious. Ahem. I meant the head, actually, not what you were thinking!

Bosses: Lagoda Vereskova, Softpaw, Poleaxe the Merciless, Fenia.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by ogres and elemental spirits.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Ah, Firefrost and its temple... An island where bitter cold and scorching flame exist in peace and harmony. A beautiful place! And everything that looks beautiful in the Astral is in fact deadly dangerous. I advise you to remember that, and to give Firefrost a wide berth. Before, only wild goblins and trolls lived there, but now, they say, the island has also been overrun by elementals. The cause, I suppose, is the recent eruption of a volcano long thought extinct. And they also say that over all of them stands a mysterious spirit, born of the two elements. I'd like to have a look at that marvel! In short, if you're not afraid of elementals and have no wish to live forever, you can find yourself a sturdy crew and give them battle. After all, it is an ancient temple, and countless riches must surely be hidden in it. It would be a sin to let such goods go to waste!

Bosses: Hestia, Bedlam, Blinder, Diamond.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate and tundra; the allod consists of four shards.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by elemental spirits and the June.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Forgotten Temple? And what, may I ask, interested you in that cursed place? Believe me, anyone who gets there will want to forget the nightmares they lived through as soon as possible. Once it was a heap of June ruins of no interest to anyone, in the middle of an islet that not even the demons cared about, but then the Wormfaces reached the temple and awakened the flame that had slumbered in the temple for centuries. The island blazed like a torch until, by a whim of fate, it collided with an icy fragment of another island. Now half of the island on which the temple stands breathes heat, while on the other half you can freeze to the bone. Besides, it is full of aggressive elementals, old but still working guardian golems, and Wormfaces who very much dislike strangers. Still, among the Historians there are madmen ready to risk their lives for knowledge. I heard that not long ago the expedition of Martin de Blizare set off for the Forgotten Temple... And nobody has heard of that expedition since!

Bosses: Glacier, Ekaterina Arhivina, Sleepless Guard, Az and Yaz.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mainly by trolls and lamias.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Far out in the Astral I once happened upon an island where eternal winter reigns. It is ruled by Yaver Arteia, a mad Arisen woman who calls herself the Snow Queen. Oh, what a vile hag she is, I tell you! I escaped from that island by a sheer miracle. The Snow Queen's favorite pastime is to abduct people and set them all manner of riddles. Fail to guess one, and you are turned into an ice statue! In her ice castle Yaver Arteia keeps whole galleries of ice sculptures that were once orcs, gibberlings, Arisen, humans... Her heart is as cold as her icy throne! That merciless shrew was all set to turn me into an ice statue too, and only by a miracle did I get away. Yaver Arteia must be stopped! If she simply killed people, fine — you'd rest a while in Purgatory, and that's that. But she turns them into statues. Just imagine: a man stands there, unable to move, to breathe, even to close his eyes. And so for a year, two, ten... Brr, how horrible. No, such cold-blooded torment cannot go unpunished! But reaching the queen will not be easy. Chill, a mad werebear shaman, faithfully guards his mistress's peace. And rumor has it that in especially fierce blizzards a huge bear named Helad appears on the island — though whether that is true is for you to find out.

Bosses: Helad, Sharptooth, Chill, Yaver Arteia.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Coba Plateau.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a goblin settlement.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do you think of goblins? On the one hand, they are unfortunate creatures. Everyone makes fun of them and despises them a little. They are the heroes of countless jokes and the pets of orc shamans. Sometimes you just feel sorry for them. And on the other hand? Thieves and bandits. Nasty pests, always ready to do something low. Ever had dealings with the arms mafia on Coba Plateau? There you go! There is a goblin island in the Astral. Their stronghold. A Republic! They even elect themselves this, what's it called... such a funny word... a president every year! For three terms running a shaman named Urub has been elected that very president. It is he who organizes the goblins' pirate raids. If in the course of your wanderings you manage to find this island — carry out the sentence and behead the goblin republic!

Bosses: Goblin Overseer, Buzz, Urub.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Tundra. Closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the grave of a June hunter.

Story:

We are met by the Fearless Family of Gibberlings. They told us that they were sent here by an elder from the Frozen Frontier to find some blood artifact that Nordrak needs so badly. It should be somewhere near the grave of the great June dragon hunter Yad-Volk (he imprisoned Nordrak on the Frozen Frontier). Along the way we try to solve the riddle of the grave: on one of the obelisks a wolf is drawn, and next to it two stones with patterns — and it is these we seek out. The first stone drops from the Yeti Leader, the second is carried by the Harpy Chieftainess. We insert these stones into the hollows of the obelisk in the center of the allod. In a snowstorm Yad-Volk and a Ghostly Dragon appear. After the victory over the dragon, we take the blood artifact from the stele and give it to the Gibberlings.

Bosses: Polar Yeti Leader, Rock Harpy Chieftainess, Ghostly Dragon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Whirl.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph and the Dragon Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by draconids.

Story:

On the island we meet a mysterious individual who tells us about his supposed exploits and says that his task is to obtain the blood of the Great Dragon. He asks us to get some practice before we go after the Great Dragon together with him, and to clear the island of draconids, killing their leader in the process. When we return victorious, the Mysterious Individual says that while we were resting and amusing ourselves with the draconids, he found out that the Great Dragon is in a cave on the other end of the island, and it is time to finish him off. After the victory, the Mysterious Individual says that we did well to defeat the Dragon, and that he, too, started out with exploits just like these and is now a great hero. In a word, showing off.

Bosses: Draconid Boss, Dragon (great).

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Oh, I would not advise you to get mixed up with the Draconids. Dangerous creatures. Even the Demon Hunters, who have made an alliance with them, do not fully trust these beings. And why is that? Because the Draconids guard their secrets like the apple of their eye! And do not trust them even to their friends. I do not know what secret is kept in the Green Maze. The Historians who tried to explore it never managed to get into its far part, access to which is closed by a magic barrier. As soon as they tried to get past it, two supreme Draconids appeared, two Guardians of the Limit, as they call themselves, and drove the Historians out. Since then the Draconids meet all uninvited guests with steel. If you have a taste for risk, you may try to uncover the secret of the Green Maze. But you will have to find your way through the ancient ruins on your own.

Bosses: Version 1: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Cursed Warrior. Version 2: Supreme Spellcaster, Supreme Healer, Reborn Warrior, Twice Born.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tropical. Closest to the Kingdom of Elements.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by fire elementals and draconids.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever heard of Volcano Isle? No? Then listen. Not long ago a tribe of draconids appeared on this island, worshipping a fire god who sleeps in the crater of a long-extinct volcano. With constant sacrifices the draconids kept him asleep, so that he would not awaken and his searing fury would not break out. But not long ago their high priest broke the established order and summoned the sleeper. The volcano awoke, and a mighty fire elemental burst out. From tongues of flame and the heat of flowing magma he created four guardians — huge fiery manticores, whose breath can burn anyone to ashes on the spot! If you decide to go to the island and try to awaken the sleeping flame, you must repeat the draconids' ritual, laying the fiery hearts of shellbacks on the altars. But don't even try to take him on while his faithful manticores are alive! The fire god put a particle of his power into each guardian, and with their death he will be greatly weakened. That's all I know about Volcano Isle. Good luck to you!

Bosses: Supreme Draconid, Bonesnapper, Hephaesto.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Zem fanatics and heretics.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

And how do you know about that, eh? That's classified information! The Committee will wring your neck for disclosing it! Oh, all right. Since you already know about the heretics themselves, so be it — I'll tell you in confidence. But mind, not a word to anyone! The Heretic Refuge is a stain on the reputation of all the Arisen. After all, it is from their people that all these dangerous madmen come! The heretics refuse to acknowledge the holiness of Nezeb, Tensess and Skrakan. They believe that everything that exists arose from four elements — fire, earth, water, and nature as the union of all three pure elements. And they are so hardened in their heresy that they accept no arguments of reason. They bitterly hate everyone who does not share their faith. After several high-profile murders committed by this sect, the Church, with the full support of the Committee and of Yasker himself, anathematized them and opened a hunt for them. The heretics — or rather the handful that remained of their sect — seized an astral ship in port and vanished into the depths of the Astral. Time passed, and their existence was simply forgotten; all the documents were classified and sent to the archive. But not long ago a captain I know told me he had heard about the heretics from someone who had seen with his own eyes a man who had the misfortune to stumble upon their refuge in the Astral. That poor wretch barely escaped! His ship was scorched by fire, a hole from a huge boulder gaped in the hold, all the rigging was covered in mold, and half the crew had turned into ice statues... So if your adventures lead you to the secret refuge of the heretics, know this — they are mad murderers, and they will try to destroy you at any cost!

Bosses: Yasskul Flach, Negus Minhotep, Negus Haifa, Negus Zirach.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao
